dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows deep eclipses on odd cycles and no dip on even cycles, with a secondary eclipse almost as deep as the primary and huge swings in depth between transits. This pattern matches a stellar binary at 28.4 days with alternating primary and secondary eclipses, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd events deep, even events ~zero, 7.8 sigma difference indicates two different dips at twice the reported period, as expected for an eclipsing binary.
Significant secondary eclipse comparable in depth to the primary confirms stellar-companion eclipses, not a planetary transit.
Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent; one transit absent and one transit ~twice the mean, consistent with odd/even binary, not a stable planet.
reasons.value: 1.696840765519991e-17 (chi2 81.20, dof 3; outliers BTJD 1931.68 depth_ppm -22 sigma -6.6, BTJD 1974.183 depth_ppm 4860 sigma 4.9)

reasons.why: Depth changes by >100% within the same pipeline, driven by the missing vs deep even transit, confirming systematics are not calibration but alternate events.
